semester: 1st Semester (Winter term start); 2nd Semester (Summer term start)

learning_outcomes.text: Students know different types of representations; know which one is useful for which purpose and target group, and can read simple standard-compliant drawings.
Students can create simple technical drawings and freehand sketches on paper.
Students can solve basic problems of descriptive geometry on paper.
Students can name basic form elements and mechanical engineering components.
Students independently perform calculations for fits and other tolerance calculations.
Students can discuss in groups and in partner work and collaboratively process tasks in a targeted manner.
Students can assess their own performance level and prior knowledge in comparison to others and independently reduce weaknesses through the learning platform.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Representations of technical structures – delimitation from CAD
Historically, according to target group and purpose, value of the sketch
Notes and exercises on perspective freehand drawing
Paper formats, line types, projection methods
The "space corner", "views", sections, developments, true sizes, penetrations
Fundamental deviations from the ideal shape:
Edges, roughness, dimensional tolerances, form and position tolerances, general tolerances
Tolerance calculations (closing dimension), ISO tolerance and fit systems
Details of the standard-compliant single-part drawing:
Drawing frame, title block, general information, special drawing entries (e.g. hardness specifications), notes on the drawing review process
Parts lists, assembly drawing, general arrangement drawing, item numbers and other special drawing entries
Purpose and origin, scopes of validity and binding nature, standard number series
teaching_methods: Tutorially supervised small groups with concrete objects (gear drives, etc.) at the start of the study/semester
Mandatory exercises in coached small groups
Homework in small groups and/or individual work

assessment_methods.method: Course achievements (SLV) in the form of semester-long assignments

assessment_rules: A passed module examination is required for credit points. Course achievements (SLV) are required for admission to the exam.
